subject: maths
question: A product priced at ₹800 is sold for ₹680. What is the percentage of discount offered?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Marked Price (MP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 800 : 680 = 20 : 17

**Discount** in units = 20 − 17 = 3 units

**Discount %** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (3 ÷ 20) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the product = **₹800**

Selling Price (SP) of the product = **₹680**

**Formula Used:**

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

Discount Percentage = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38173e6b9eb11992c6403f513c6a676fd7cf5e617587c75a5488a00d5d9bed51.png] 

⇒ Discount = 800 − 680

⇒ Discount = 120

⇒ Discount Percentage = (120 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ Discount Percentage = (12 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Discount Percentage = 0.15 × 100

⇒ Discount Percentage = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The **Marked Price** is the price at which a product is listed by the retailer or manufacturer before any discount.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts of a% and b% are given, the **Effective Discount** = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Profit and Loss Relation

The relationship between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)** is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
